title: Heterostructuring as Gateway to Electron Doping of Nickelate Superconductors
authors: Chao Deng, Motoharu Kitatani, Guiwen Jiang, Siqi Guo, Niklas Witt, Ao Zhang, Wenfeng Wu, Mi Jiang, Karsten Held, Liang Si
abstract: Despite enormous expenditures in the research field, the electron-doped side of nickelate superconductors remains uncharted territory. Substituting the trivalent rare-earth cations by a tetravalent one hitherto failed. Here, we demonstrate by first-principles calculations a disorder-free route to electron dope Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates. When intercalating wide-band-gap insulating layers such as La$X$O$_3$ ($X$=Al, Ga, Sc) into La$_2$NiO$_4$, the extra (LaO)$^+$ layers act as electron donors, releasing carriers into the Ni-3$d$ orbitals. This electron doping puts La$_2$NiO$_4$:La$_2$AlO$_4$ naturally in the optimal region for $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave superconductivity with T$_c$ exceeding 50 K. The same concept also allows us to electron dope La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, the superconductor in the limelight.
summary: The authors propose using heterostructuring—specifically intercalating wide-band-gap insulators into nickelates—as a novel, disorder-free way to achieve electron doping. Theoretical calculations predict that this process drives the material into an optimal superconducting state, yielding high critical temperatures for these complex oxides.
main_problem: Electron-doping of nickelate superconductors remains an uncharted territory, and conventional substitutional doping methods have proven insufficient.
main_result: The intercalation of wide-band-gap insulators creates a disorder-free route to electron-doped nickelates, predicting high-$T_c$ $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave superconductivity exceeding 50 K in $	ext{La}_2	ext{NiO}_4:	ext{La}_2	ext{AlO}_4$.
method: The study relies heavily on first-principles calculations, including DFT and advanced many-body techniques like DMFT, D$\Gamma$A, and FLEX.
model_or_system: The focus is on Ruddlesden–Popper nickelates ($	ext{R}_{n+1}	ext{Ni}_n	ext{O}_{3n+1}$) and their engineered heterostructures formed by intercalating insulating layers like $	ext{LaXO}_3$ into $	ext{La}_2	ext{NiO}_4$.
key_observables: Electron doping level (charge transfer), $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$), and orbital occupations ($	ext{Ni}-t_{2g}$ and $	ext{Ni}-e_g$).
important_parameters: $T_c > 50 	ext{ K}$ for the engineered heterostructures; ambient pressure stability.
main_assumptions: The superconducting properties are predicted based on theoretical models (D$\Gamma$A) and assume structural/thermodynamic stability of the resulting superlattices.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the intercalation mechanism, showing charge transfer into $	ext{Ni}-3d$ orbitals, and present band structures confirming orbital shifts in the heterostructures.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem (electron doping difficulty), proposes the solution (heterostructuring via intercalation), details the theoretical framework using multiple advanced calculations, presents results showing successful electron doping and high $T_c$, and confirms structural stability.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental questions in strongly correlated materials physics by proposing a chemically clean method to tune carrier concentration, which is crucial for understanding unconventional superconductivity mechanisms.
